what_was_done.action: Used `type ReconcilerActionRefusedPayload = {...}` (type alias, not interface) so it assigns cleanly to `PipelineEvent.payload: Record<string, unknown>`.
what_was_done.result: TypeScript treats interfaces as 'open' (declaration-mergeable) and rejects assignment to closed Record index signatures even when all property values are compatible. Type alias is closed → assigns cleanly. Tested empirically: switched from `interface` to `type` cleared 3 TS errors (event-log.ts:129, event-log.test.ts:220, event-log.test.ts:409).

deviations_from_ac: None on the bead's literal ACs. Note on field-naming: bead description's 'structured fields' list includes `at` as a separate field, but the bead also says 'Schema mirrors existing reconciler-action-taken' and the existing PipelineEvent shape uses `timestamp` at the top level. Implementation maps `at` → `timestamp` (single field on the wire) per parity-with-existing-variants principle; rationale + mapping documented inline in the ReconcilerActionRefusedEvent interface JSDoc. No double-write; consumers reading `e.timestamp` get the refusal time. Wave 3 callers building these events pass `timestamp` (or omit it for `now`) per the existing appendEvent contract.
surprises_or_findings: 1) PipelineEvent is NOT a discriminated union in the strict TypeScript sense — `type: string` is open-ended (not a literal union). The bead description's 'discriminated union' phrasing is loose. This means: (a) additive variants cannot break exhaustiveness anywhere in the codebase (zero risk on the Risk Flag's switch-statement watch); (b) the new typed sub-interface gives Wave 3 (ehp.4-ehp.10) a strongly-typed import target without imposing constraints on existing callers. 2) Switching from interface to type alias was required for TS index-signature compatibility — interfaces are 'open' (declaration-mergeable) and don't satisfy `Record<string, unknown>` even when all properties are unknown-compatible. Type aliases are 'closed' and assign cleanly. Documented inline so future edits don't accidentally revert. 3) Stale test discovery: stuck-in-stage.test.ts has 2 pre-existing failures (tests expect STAGE_RESUME_ACTIONS-style dispatch; source moved to run-coherence-agent at wlsr.14 per ADR-015). Confirmed pre-existing via empirical stash-baseline re-run. Not in ehp.2 scope to fix; flagging for QA.

recommendation_for_next: Wave 2 (beads_web-ehp.3) is the next bead in the ehp epic — it owns the `RefusalCode` enum and `buildDispatchContext` / `evaluatePreconditions` library. ehp.3 should import RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED and ReconcilerActionRefusedPayload from this bead's exports as the canonical event-construction target. Wave 3 (ehp.4-ehp.10) integrate at each reconciler rule's act(); each rule will: (1) build DispatchContext, (2) call evaluatePreconditions, (3) on refusal: appendEvent({type: RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED, epicId, correlationId, payload: {ruleName, action, refusalCode, failedCheck, reason}}) and return without dispatching. The typed payload + typed event interface defined here ensure each Wave 3 callsite has compile-time safety on the field shape.
